sentences.text: This application is filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short, BNSS), seeking regular bail.
2. The applicant is the sole accused in Crime No.139/2026 of Pazhayannur Police Station, Thrissur District.

The offences alleged are punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 506 and 451 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3.
The prosecution case, in short, is that the de facto complainant had acquaintance with the applicant while he worked at the KSEB Office at Pazhayannur, during the period of 2017-18.

It is alleged that on 06.03.2021 at 10 p.m., the applicant trespassed into the bed room of the de facto complainant, forcefully pushed her on the cot, committed rape, recorded naked pictures of the de facto complainant and threatened the de facto complainant that if she disclosed the incident to anyone, he will show the naked pictures of the de facto complainant to all, forcefully inserted his penis into the mouth of the de facto BAIL APPL.
OF 2026 2026:KER:29574 complainant

and citing the possession of naked photographs of the de facto complainant, he further committed rape on the de facto complainant on 14.03.2023, 14.09.2023, 20.09.2023, 27.09.2023 and also on other dates and time at the house of the de facto complainant at Vadakkethara and thereby committed the offences.
4. I have heard Sri. N.Sunil Joseph, the learned counsel for the applicant and Smt. Sreeja.V, the learned Senior Public Prosecutor.
Perused the case diary.
5. The learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The counsel further submitted that no materials are on record to connect the applicant with the alleged crime; hence, he is entitled to bail.

On the other hand, the learned Senior Public Prosecutor submitted that the alleged incident occurred as a part of the intentional criminal acts of the applicant, and he is not entitled to bail at this stage.
6. The applicant was remanded to judicial BAIL APPL. NO. 1849 OF 2026 2026:KER:29574 custody on 23.03.2026.
The investigation is almost over.
The applicant is aged 42 years and the victim is aged 54 years.
The victim is a divorcee.
As per the FI Statement, there were several instances of physical relationship between the applicant and the victim.
According to the victim, those were forceful in nature.
The first sexual intercourse was on 06.03.2021 and the last specified one was on 27.09.2023.
However, the complaint was filed only on 01.03.2026.
There is no explanation for the delay.
That apart, in between, another crime was registered against the applicant in the year 2025 at the instance of the victim, as evident from Annexure A2 FIR.
The allegation in the said crime is of cheating with regard to some chitty transactions between the victim and the applicant.

There is Vincent Mathew vs State Of Kerala on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199609904/
2 absolutely no allegation of rape or sexual assault in the said crime.

sentences.text: The applicant has no criminal antecedents.
For these reasons, I do not find any reason to hold that the continued detention of the applicant is required for any purpose.
Hence, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
BAIL APPL. NO. 1849 OF 2026 2026:KER:29574

In the result, the application is allowed on the following conditions: -
(i) The applicant shall be released on bail on executing a bond for Rs.1,00,000/-
(Rupees One lakh only) with two solvent sureties for the like sum each to the satisfaction of the jurisdictional Magistrate/Court.
(ii) The applicant shall fully co-operate with the investigation.
(iii) The applicant shall appear before the investigating officer between 10.00 a.m and 11.00 a.m. every Saturday until further orders.
He shall also appear before the investigating officer as and when required.
(iv) The applicant shall not commit any offence of a like nature while on bail.

(v) The applicant shall not attempt to contact any of the prosecution witnesses,
directly or through any other person, or in any other way try to tamper with the evidence or influence any witnesses or other persons related to the investigation.
(vi) The applicant shall not leave the State of BAIL APPL. NO. 1849 OF 2026 2026:KER:29574 Kerala without the permission of the trial Court.
(vii) The application, if any, for deletion/modification of the bail conditions or cancellation of bail on the grounds of violating the bail conditions shall be filed at the jurisdictional court.
Sd/-
DR. KAUSER EDAPPAGATH JUDGE ARK BAIL APPL.
